nonblocking_findings: R-A-1 / Review B F1 (review-a, review-b): isAllowed joins a relative path with snapshot.root, but commitDecision and turnProblems receive git-root paths. Review B probed the effect: the guard denies too much only, so the item is fail-closed. Carry to tech-debt at closeout.
README code span (review-a, review-c): plugins/opencode-measure-guard/README.md line 98 opens a code span with two backticks and closes it with one. Cosmetic only. Carry to tech-debt at closeout.

X2 no-op (adversarial F1): the X2 mutation in test-strategy.md section 4.6 changes no result because isAllowed already calls joinPath on both sides. The effective form is caught by B5 and V11. Defect in the mutation list, not in shipped code. Carry to tech-debt at closeout.

O(n^2) dedupe (adversarial F2): parseAllowList uses folders.includes in a forEach, so a 50 000-entry list costs seconds per parse. Availability only on an operator-owned file. Carry to tech-debt at closeout.

Wide legal entries (review-b F2): an operator entry such as .git/ would let an agent write into .git without a [~] task. The spec keeps such entries legal. Report to the user at closeout; carry to tech-debt.

Binary or large list files (review-b F3): readAllow accepts any bytes; a binary line that ends with / becomes a folder entry, and a 50 000-line list slows each guarded call. Availability only. Carry to tech-debt at closeout.
